title: Review of c29's kernel-drive ringed cells (SIBMD): replicated on fresh seed 5 at 256^2 (L ring 1.56, 235 persistent splits, gen 6, 56 ringed swimmers >= 3 BL), but only one track swims >= 3 BL with its ring and then divides (3.16 BL)
summary: I re-ran the claimed world with WORLD_P {drive: kernel, mu: 1.0, kd: 0.08, chi: 5} on fresh seed 5 at 256^2 with labkit (t=10000) and with c29's ringtrack.py and lineage_report.py (T=10000). labkit: from noise (first frame), L link rim/core 1.56, rim/out 8.25, 856/1206 individuals membrane-like; 235 persistent splits, max generation 6, merge/split 0.19; 143 tracks move >= 1 BL, max 3.7. ringtrack: contour ring >= 1.5 in 94.3% of 8809 cell-frames (median 1.67), 63 persistent splits, 56 tracks swim >= 3 BL and all 56 hold the ring in >= half their frames; one track (#74, t=1000-1940, a founder formed from noise) swims 3.16 BL with ring median 1.62 and divides into #228 and #229, and #228 then swims 4.43 BL with its ring. The sheet shows the claimed history: ringed crescents swim and divide during colonization and jam into a static lattice by t~6000. I read world.py: L is made only by the cell's catalyst (b K S, K held by phi^2 mobility), so the chi-drift ring counts under the L3 quasi-equilibrium clause; the kernel drive uses no per-body label.

seeds_run.note: 1 same-track swim+ring+divide (3.16 BL), at the margin

verdicts.limitation: The same-individual evidence is thin: 1 track on my seed (3.16 BL, just over the gate) against 1-3 on the claim's seeds, and all of it during colonization before the lattice jams by t~6000. Motion and division are mostly in different individuals. No Laplacian-only twin, so not diffusion-tested.
